source: Kocsis & Szepesvari (2006) Bandit based Monte-Carlo planning
finding: UCT applies the UCB1 bandit rule to each tree node. Proven consistent. On random P-game trees it converges like alpha-beta.
numbers: Theorem 6: bias O(log n / n), root failure probability falls at a polynomial rate (bias terms multiplied by horizon D). P-games: iterations to reach low failure rate grow about B^(D/2), same order as alpha-beta; B=2,D=20 and B=8,D=8 tested. Plain MC and minimax-MC (MMMC) converge to non-zero failure; MMMC worse than MC.
limits: Synthetic domains only. Proof assumes bias scaled by D. Authors note the bound might be unimprovable.
agent_relevance: Explore/exploit via UCB at each choice point is a sound control rule when rollouts are cheap and rewards bounded. Our agent has costly, noisy rollouts, so the guarantee is only a guide.

source: Kocsis & Szepesvari (2006) Bandit based Monte-Carlo planning (sailing domain)
finding: In the sailing stochastic shortest-path task UCT needed far fewer samples than ARTDP and PG-ID to reach error 0.1.
numbers: Grid sizes 2x2 to 40x40 tested; samples needed to reach error below 0.1 plotted; UCT scaled best with problem size and could solve larger problems.
limits: Single synthetic MDP with a simulator. No real games in this paper.
agent_relevance: Evidence that selective sampling beats uniform or breadth-first allocation as the space grows.

source: Silver et al. (2017) Mastering Chess and Shogi by Self-Play with a General RL Algorithm (AlphaZero)
finding: MCTS guided by a learned policy and value network beat the top alpha-beta engines while searching far fewer positions.
numbers: 100-game matches, 1 min per move: chess vs Stockfish AlphaZero 28 wins, 72 draws, 0 losses (white 25W/25D, black 3W/47D). Shogi vs Elmo 90 wins, 2 draws, 8 losses. Search speed 80 thousand positions/s in chess vs about 70 million for Stockfish. Beat Stockfish after 4 hours (300k steps), Elmo after under 2 hours; 5,000 TPUs for self-play.
limits: Hardware gap (4 TPUs vs engine CPU) and time control were disputed outside the paper. Closed rules and perfect simulator.
agent_relevance: Value-and-prior-guided search needs far fewer node visits than blind search. Our LLM prior and value judge play the same roles.

source: Silver et al. (2017) AlphaZero vs AlphaGo Zero in Go
finding: AlphaZero with the same generic MCTS settings also beat the 3-day AlphaGo Zero.
numbers: 100 games: 60 wins, 40 losses for AlphaZero (31-19 as white, 29-21 as black; derived from table). Same hyper-parameters reused across all three games.
limits: Margin in Go is modest; AlphaZero trained for a shorter time than AG0 3-day.
agent_relevance: Generic search settings transfer across tasks when the prior and value are learned. A prompted judge may not match a trained value.

source: Schrittwieser et al. (2020) Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model (MuZero)
finding: MCTS over a learned latent model, no rules given, matched AlphaZero in board games and set a state of the art on 57 Atari games.
numbers: 800 simulations per search in board games, 50 in Atari. Beat R2D2 in 42 of 57 games and SimPLe in all 57. In Go, planning scaled to two orders of magnitude longer searches than used in training; in Atari performance stayed stable and decreased only slightly at much longer searches. Reanalyze variant re-runs MCTS on old data for sample efficiency.
limits: Atari scaling flatter than Go, attributed to model inaccuracy. Needs heavy training.
agent_relevance: Search value depends on model quality: when the world model is poor (as an LLM simulator can be), more simulations help less.

source: Hao et al. (2023) Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP), Blocksworld
finding: Using the LLM as both world model and policy inside MCTS lifts Blocksworld planning from near zero to a majority of cases.
numbers: LLaMA-33B success 2/4/6-step: CoT 0.17/0.02/0.00, CoT pass@10 0.23/0.07/0.00, RAP(10) 1.00/0.86/0.26, RAP(20) 1.00/0.88/0.42; paper reports 64% average and a 33% relative gain over CoT with GPT-4 (0.50/0.63/0.40).
limits: Small benchmark subset, LLaMA-33B. RAP reward hand-chosen. The reward for a step hides history so late steps are easier.
agent_relevance: MCTS with a self-simulated world model gives lookahead without training. Gain comes from retrying after dead ends.

source: Hao et al. (2023) RAP, GSM8K and PrOntoQA
finding: On math and logic RAP beat chain-of-thought with self-consistency, but gains were small on GSM8K.
numbers: GSM8K: RAP 48.8% (single trace by reward), about 3 points more with RAP-Aggregate, above CoT and Least-to-Most self-consistency. PrOntoQA: prediction accuracy 94.2%, proof accuracy 78.8%, 14 points over CoT on proof, 4.4 over CoT-SC on prediction; 20 MCTS iterations vs 20 SC samples. Ablation: action-likelihood reward essential for planning, not helpful for math.
limits: Reward design is task-specific and tuned by heuristics. Compute not matched beyond iteration count.
agent_relevance: Reward choice (self-evaluation, confidence, likelihood) changes results; one fixed reward does not transfer.

source: Hao et al. (2023) RAP, full Blocksworld with Llama-2 70B
finding: On the 602-case full Blocksworld, RAP(10) kept high success at 6+ steps where CoT collapsed.
numbers: Easy setting CoT 0.49/0.18/0.06 vs RAP(10) 1.00/0.99/0.75 at 2/4/6 steps; Hard setting CoT 0.22/0.14/0.02 vs RAP 0.67/0.76/0.74.
limits: Easy setting uses known minimum plan length for demonstrations. Table partly garbled in text extraction for 8-12 steps.
agent_relevance: Search matters most as plans get longer; a plain chain degrades with depth.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts, Game of 24 (GPT-4)
finding: Breadth-limited search over LLM-proposed and LLM-valued thoughts beat sampling by a wide margin. This is BFS, not MCTS, but it is the baseline later MCTS work compares to.
numbers: 100 games: IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC k=100 9.0%, CoT best-of-100 49%, ToT b=1 45%, ToT b=5 74%. Crosswords: word-level 60% vs below 16% for baselines, 4 of 20 games solved.
limits: No backup or exploration bonus. Prompted value judgments are noisy; depth is 3 for Game of 24.
agent_relevance: Even greedy tree search (b=1) beats 100 blind samples. Search beats best-of-N when intermediate steps can be judged.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Language Agent Tree Search (LATS), HumanEval and WebShop
finding: MCTS with LLM value, self-consistency score, environment feedback and reflection improved agent tasks.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 with GPT-4: base 80.1, Reflexion 91.0, LATS 92.7 (5 children, 8 iterations). WebShop (GPT-3.5, 50 instructions): ReAct 53.8 score / 28.0% SR, Reflexion 64.2 / 35.0, LATS 75.9 / 38.0; fine-tuned 67.5 / 45.0; human expert 82.1 / 59.6.
limits: WebShop SR still below fine-tuning and humans. Needs states that can be reverted. Small test sets (50 WebShop tasks).
agent_relevance: Gain over Reflexion is 1.7 points on HumanEval but 11.7 score points on WebShop; search helps most where the first answer is wrong.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) LATS, HotPotQA and Game of 24 ablations
finding: Every LATS component mattered. Replacing MCTS with DFS cost 0.21 exact match.
numbers: HotPotQA EM (n=5, k=50): LATS 0.63, no reflection 0.58, DFS 0.42, no LM heuristic 0.37, RAP(ReAct) 0.54, ToT(ReAct) 0.49; ReAct best-of-250 0.42; LATS n=1,k=50 0.48. Game of 24 (GPT-3.5): CoT 0.08, Reflexion 0.12, ToT 0.20, RAP 0.40, LATS 0.44.
limits: Authors' own ablations. ReAct versions of ToT and RAP did worse than their reasoning-only versions on HotPotQA.
agent_relevance: Selection plus backup (the MCTS part) beat DFS and best-of-k at equal trajectory counts; value from the LM matters most.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) LATS, cost and failure modes
finding: LATS costs more calls than ReAct but used fewer nodes than ToT and RAP when it succeeded. Reflections in WebShop were often generic.
numbers: Token consumption upon success: RAP 210,215, LATS 176,500 (Table 9); nodes at k=10 on HotPotQA: ToT 33.97, RAP 31.53, LATS 28.42 as printed (column order partly garbled), EM 0.34 / 0.44 / 0.44.
limits: Authors say reflections are generic and the agent gets stuck in local minima; method needs environment rollback.
agent_relevance: Plan for token cost and for state reversion; generic self-reflection is weak feedback.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Mutual Reasoning Makes Smaller LLMs Stronger Problem-Solvers (rStar)
finding: MCTS with human-like reasoning actions plus a second model that checks mutual consistency lifted small models sharply on GSM8K.
limits: Gain over SC@128 small for the strongest model (Phi3-mini 88.68 vs 90.67). Part of gain is the discriminator, not search alone (generator@maj only 27.22 on LLaMA2-7B).
agent_relevance: Search alone helps modestly; verification by agreement with a second model carries a large share.

source: Wang et al. (2024) rStar, rollouts and RAP saturation
finding: rStar gained even at 2 rollouts. RAP saturated and even fell after 4 rollouts on LLaMA3-8B-Instruct.
numbers: Self-consistency and rStar both kept improving with more rollouts. Paper says only 24% of trajectories from LLaMA2-7B on GSM8K under RAP were correct (as stated in the introduction).
limits: Run on GSM8K; authors attribute the RAP decline to a weak reward and action space.
agent_relevance: More simulations do not always help: a poor value signal makes extra search noise.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) ReST-MCTS*: LLM Self-Training via Process Reward Guided Tree Search
finding: MCTS* trains a step value model from tree search with no human step labels; the value model gave small gains as a verifier.
numbers: Verification over 256 outputs, Mistral-7B MetaMATH: GSM8K SC 83.9, ORM 86.2, SC+ORM 86.6, MATH-SHEPHERD 87.1, SC+MS 86.3, SC+ReST-MCTS value 87.5; MATH500 35.1 / 36.4 / 38.0 / 37.3 / 38.3 / 39.0.
limits: Margins of 0.4 to 0.7 points over MATH-SHEPHERD; no variance reported in the table. Self-training gains vary by backbone.
agent_relevance: Learned step values from search are a usable but modest verifier; do not expect large verifier gains.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) Accessing GPT-4 level Mathematical Olympiad Solutions via MCT Self-Refine (MCTSr)
finding: MCTS over whole answers, with the LLM refining and self-rating each node, improved LLaMA3-8B with more rollouts.
numbers: LLaMA3-8B GSM8K (1319 problems): zero-shot CoT 74.07%, one-turn self-refine 86.96%, MCTSr 4 rollouts 93.03%, 8 rollouts 96.66%. GSM-Hard: 25.47 / 33.36 / 39.88 / 45.49. A 5000-problem MATH table rises from 40.60 to 77.40.
limits: Authors note a ceiling on GSM-Hard at higher rollouts. Self-rating is by the same model, so scores may be inflated; not independently replicated here.
agent_relevance: Self-refine plus MCTS gives clear gains, but LLM self-reward can be biased; test with an external check.

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
finding: Compared best-of-N, beam search and lookahead search (an MCTS special case without stochastic elements) against a PRM on MATH.
numbers: Budget up to 256 generations. At low budget beam search best; as budget grew its gains shrank and it fell below best-of-N; lookahead generally underperformed at equal generation budget. On easy questions (bins 1-2) beam search over-optimised the PRM at high budget; on medium (bins 3-4) it beat best-of-N. Compute-optimal allocation matched best-of-N with about 4x less compute.
limits: Authors did not run full MCTS; they argue lookahead represents it. PaLM 2 models, PRM trained without human labels.
agent_relevance: Match search method to difficulty: use search on medium problems, parallel sampling on easy ones. Exploit-heavy search over a learned value can overfit.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference (REBASE)
finding: At equal compute, MCTS lost to plain sampling with weighted voting on MATH500 and GSM8K. A simpler reward-balanced tree search (REBASE) won.
numbers: MCTS uses dozens of times more generated tokens than sampling. Mistral-7B MATH500: sampling 256 samples 8.70e14 FLOPs 42.8%; REBASE 32 samples 1.36e14 FLOPs 45.0%. Llemma-7B: 45.5% (1.0e15) vs 46.8% (1.48e14); paper states about 7x less compute. Llemma-7B with REBASE beat Llemma-34B across budgets.
limits: Open models of 7B to 34B; MCTS configuration is a baseline with UCT constant set in appendix B, not tuned heavily. Table rows partly garbled in extraction.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that vanilla UCT rollouts waste budget in LLM settings; cheap value-guided allocation is better.

source: Feng et al. (2023) Alphazero-like Tree-Search can Guide Large Language Model Decoding and Training (TS-LLM)
finding: Learned value function with MCTS-alpha matched simple value search on shallow tasks and clearly beat it on deep ones.
numbers: Path@1: GSM8K CoT-greedy 41.4, BFS-V 52.5, MCTS-alpha 51.9, MCTS-Rollout 47.8 (3.4k tokens); Game24 12.7 / 64.8 / 63.3 / 71.3; PrOntoQA 48.8 / 94.4 / 99.4 / 96.9; Chess endgame win rate 57.8 / 61.8 / 96.90 / 98.76; RLHF reward 0.318 / -1.295 / 2.221 / 1.925. Tree depth reached 64 vs 10 in ToT and 7 in RAP.
limits: Authors: backup helps only on deep-search problems. Needs training a value network.
agent_relevance: Selection and backup earn their cost only on long-horizon tasks; short reasoning chains do not need them.

source: Feng et al. (2023) TS-LLM, prompted vs learned value
finding: Prompted LLM value (as in ToT) was far worse than a learned value function.
numbers: Game24 with LLaMA-SFT policy: LLaMA prompt value 9.2, GPT-3.5 prompt value 21.0, learned value 64.8; with GPT-3.5 policy 15.5 (GPT-3.5 value) vs 19.1 (learned). GSM8K LLaMA-SFT: 37.4 / 45.8 / 52.5.
limits: Learned value needs labelled search data; table text extraction partly garbled so row mapping is inferred.
agent_relevance: Do not trust a prompted self-evaluation as MCTS value; ground it with checks or tools where possible.

source: Feng et al. (2023) TS-LLM, aggregation and self-improvement
finding: At equal tokens, simple self-consistency still beat tree search on GSM8K. Iterating policy and value training raised accuracy.
numbers: CoT-SC only beat TS-LLM on GSM8K at equal tokens; tree search gained less from aggregation on small problems. GSM8K accuracy rose from 51.9 to 56.5 after updating both policy and value.
limits: Authors give two reasons: smaller search space and double use of the value. Open question on scaling tree aggregation.
agent_relevance: On small problems a wide sample is a hard baseline to beat; always compare at equal tokens.

source: Liao et al. (2024) AlphaMath Almost Zero: Process Supervision without Process
finding: A policy-value model trained from MCTS data; at inference MCTS was best but slowest, step-level beam search was a cheap approximation.
numbers: MATH: greedy 53.62; maj@5 61.84; step-level beam search B1=1 62.80, B1=2 64.66, B1=3 66.30. MCTS (40 simulations) scored higher than SBS(B1=1) but took the longest time and most steps; larger beam shortened solve time.
limits: MCTS needs 40 simulations per problem, hard to use in production per authors.
agent_relevance: Beam search guided by value is the practical substitute for full MCTS at inference.

source: Tian et al. (2024) Toward Self-Improvement of LLMs via Imagination, Searching, and Criticizing (AlphaLLM)
finding: MCTS with options, state merging, fast rollout and three critics improved math without extra labels.
numbers: Llama-2-70b on GSM8K 57.8 to 92.0; WizardMath-70B on MATH 20.7 to 51.0 (self-improved plus search). GSM8K ablation: accuracy rose 79.5, 84.9, 85.9, 86.5, 87.0, 88.9 as components were added. MATH: option-level MCTS 45.4 with 148 rollouts vs sentence-level 44.1 with 198 rollouts; tool-augmented ORM removed gave 38.8.
limits: Ablation order fixed, so component gains are order-dependent. Uses a fast rollout model trained on ground truth.
agent_relevance: Coarser actions (options) cut rollouts by about a quarter and gave better scores: use step-sized actions.

source: Guan et al. (2025) rStar-Math: Small LLMs Can Master Math Reasoning with Self-Evolved Deep Thinking
finding: Four rounds of MCTS-based self-evolution produced 7B-class models matching o1-preview on MATH.
numbers: MATH: Qwen2.5-Math-7B 58.8 to 90.0 (89.4 with 8 trajectories), Phi3-mini 41.4 to 86.4; o1-preview 85.5, o1-mini 90.0. AIME 2024: 53.3% (8 of 15) vs o1-preview 44.6. Trained on 747k problems with MCTS Q-values and a process preference model.
limits: Heavy training pipeline; contamination and compute cost not evaluated by the paper.
agent_relevance: Search at inference plus a trained step scorer reaches near frontier math; but it is training, not a pure scaffold.

source: Koh et al. (2024) Tree Search for Language Model Agents
finding: Best-first tree search over an agent actions with an LLM value function raised web task success. This is not MCTS, but it is the closest search inside an agent loop.
numbers: VisualWebArena GPT-4o 18.9% to 26.4% (+39.7% relative); WebArena 15.0% to 19.2% (+28.0%); Llama-3-70B 7.6 to 10.1 on WA. Search budget on a subset: no search 24.5%, c=5 32.0%, c=20 37.0%. Depth 5, branching 5.
limits: Search needs the ability to backtrack in the environment; budgets capped for cost; absolute success still below 40%.
agent_relevance: Even five node expansions per step gave a 30% relative gain; search budget is a direct accuracy dial.

source: Antoniades et al. (2024) SWE-Search: Enhancing Software Agents with MCTS and Iterative Refinement
finding: MCTS with UCT plus depth bonus and penalty improved SWE-bench Lite resolve rates across five models.
numbers: Resolve rate adapted baseline to SWE-Search: GPT-4o 25.7 to 31.0, GPT-4o-mini 13.0 to 17.0, Qwen-2.5-72b 18.0 to 24.7, DeepSeek-V2.5 16.3 to 21.0, Llama-3.1-70b 13.6 to 17.7; mean relative gain 23% as reported. Max 100 iterations, 3 expansions per node.
limits: Single benchmark; gains grow with iteration budget but cost rises; verification relies on a model-based discriminator.
agent_relevance: UCT with added depth terms works in an agent loop; shows tuning of exploration by depth.

source: Zhang et al. (2023) Planning with Large Language Models for Code Generation (PG-TD)
finding: MCTS over token generation with test-case pass rate as reward gave small gains over sampling plus filtering.
numbers: APPS introductory, GPT-2, pass rate: beam search 11.95, sampling+filtering 25.19, SMCG-TD 24.10, PG-TD (c=4) 26.70; all with at most 256 generations.
limits: Gain over sampling plus filtering about 1.5 points; strict accuracy rows noisy; small fine-tuned GPT-2 and GPT-Neo only.
agent_relevance: With a real test-based reward, MCTS beats beam but only edges out a strong sampling baseline.

source: Zhao et al. (2023) Large Language Models as Commonsense Knowledge for Large-Scale Task Planning (LLM-MCTS)
finding: LLM used as both prior policy and world model inside PUCT beat the LLM as plain policy and plain UCT in VirtualHome.
numbers: GPT-3.5-MCTS beat GPT-3.5 Policy and fine-tuned GPT-2 policy on simple, novel and compositional tasks, with the largest margin on compositional tasks; plain UCT performed poorly in all conditions because the search tree was too large. 30-step limit.
limits: Exact success rates not read from the tables this session. Authors give minimum description length as the rule of thumb.
agent_relevance: LLM prior to prune the tree is what makes MCTS tractable; plain UCT with an LLM is not enough.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
finding: Repeated sampling with a verifier is a strong rival to search. Coverage grows roughly log-linearly with samples.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite with DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct: 15.9% with 1 sample to 56% with 250, above the 43% single-sample SOTA. CodeContests with Gemma-2B: 0.02% with 1 sample to 7.1% with 10,000. Without automatic verifiers, majority vote and reward models plateau beyond several hundred samples.
limits: No tree structure; gains need a cheap exact verifier.
agent_relevance: Where an exact check exists, plain sampling may beat MCTS; search adds value when partial progress can be scored.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Marco-o1: Towards Open Reasoning Models for Open-Ended Solutions
finding: MCTS with a reward from the model own token-probability confidence, plus step and mini-step actions.
numbers: MGSM English +6.17% and Chinese +5.60% accuracy over the base. Reward is the average over the rollout of a softmax confidence on token log-probabilities.
limits: Gains reported vs a base model, not a compute-matched sampling baseline; confidence is not correctness.
agent_relevance: Confidence-based reward is cheap but risky; pair with a checker.

source: Xie et al. (2024) Monte Carlo Tree Search Boosts Reasoning via Iterative Preference Learning
finding: MCTS used to generate step-level preference pairs for DPO training, not at inference.
numbers: Mistral-7B SFT baseline raised on GSM8K to 81.8% (+5.9), MATH 34.7% (+5.8), ARC-C 76.4% (+15.8).
limits: Training-time use; theory says on-policy data matters.
agent_relevance: Search can be used to produce better training or critique data; for a no-training scaffold only the inference-time part applies.
